test_title: RRB Group D 2025 Previous Year Numerical Qs Set - 01
subject: general
question:
A body weighs 60 kg wt on the surface of the moon. What will be the mass and the weight, respectively, of the body on the surface of the Earth?

(Take the value of g on Earth as 10 m/s²)
solution:
The correct answer is __**360 kg and 360 kg wt**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Weight changes with gravity, but mass remains the same everywhere.
 
• On the Moon: Weight = 60 kg-wt
 
• Since the Moon's gravity is 1/6 of Earth's gravity, 
 
 
• Weight on Earth = 6× Weight on Moon
 
• = 6 × 60 = 360 Kg-Wt
 
 
 
• Now, A **kilogram-weight (kg-wt) represents the gravitational pull of the Earth on a mass of 1 kg**.
 
• For this question, 1 kg-wt is equal to 10N. (g on Earth 10 m/s²)
 
 
• 360 Kg-Wt = 360 × 10 = 3600N. (Convert to SI un it)
 
 
 
• 
 Mass = weight on Earth / acceleration due to gravity on Earth

 
 
• 
 ​Mass = 3600/10 = 360 kg
 
 
 
 
• 
 Hence, the correct answer is,

 
 
• 
 Mass on Earth = 360 kg
 
 
• 
 Weight on Earth = 360 kg-wt
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mass:**

 
 
• It is the **intrinsic property** of a body that determines its **inertia**.
 
• The **S.I. unit** of mass is the **kilogram (kg)**.
 
• It is a **scalar quantity**, meaning it has only magnitude and no direction. It remains the same on **Earth**, the **Moon**, or even in **outer space**.
 
 
 
• **Weight:**
 
 
• It is the **gravitational force** acting on an object. The formula is **W = m x g**, where **m** is mass and **g** is the **acceleration due to gravity**.
 
• The **S.I. unit** of weight is the **Newton (N)**, but it is often expressed in **kg wt** for practical purposes.
 
• It is a **vector quantity** because it always acts vertically downwards towards the center of the planet.
